page.layout: One column of running text on one printed page, with a small italic verse quotation set within it. Running head at the top, page number 40 at the top left. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: „ enim præclarius, quàm ho-noribus & Reipub. muneri-bus perfunctum senem, pos-se suo iure dicere, idem quod „ apud Enniū dicit ille Pythius „ Apollo: Se esse eum, unde si-„ bi, si non populi & reges, at „ omnes sui ciues consiliū ex-„ petant?

p.i: „ Suarum rerum incerti, quos ego mea ope ex „ Incertis certos, compotesq; confilij „ Dimitto, ut ne res temerè tractent turbidas.

main_text.p: „ Est enim sine dubio domus „ Iurisconsulti, totius Oracu-„ lum ciuitatis. Quinetiam eo dem libro Antonius aliquā-to pòst, etsi Iurisconsultorū glorię subinuidés, tamen ita „ loquitur: Etenim sine con-„ trouersia & magna est ars il-la,

page.notes: Running head is set in letterspaced small capitals and could not be read reliably. The printed quotation marks („) at line starts are reproduced as printed. The verse quotation in the middle is set in smaller italic type within the text block, so it is treated as part of the text rather than a note. "Enniū" carries a tilde over the u for the omitted m. The text continues onto the next page mid-sentence.
